scope: reports/** (7,957 tracked paths, 94.9% of the repository), excluding reports/repository_audit/** which is this audit's own output
note: Nothing under reports/ is ignored except reports/content_packages/images/ (.gitignore:27). Everything a run writes there therefore becomes a candidate for the next `git add`. src/run/code_identity.py:34-43 states the repository's own position: reports/ and data/ are output roots a run legitimately dirties, which is why tracked run output is defensible in principle — but the boundary was never drawn, and 7,796 of these paths are test debris. Bulk groups below are genuinely uniform: one producer, one consumer, one method, which the reviewer can check against the cited source lines.

entries.purpose: 6 visibility packages, reports/content_packages/vis_00N_generated.json — the generated payload of each Visibility Intelligence run, one per item drained from visibility_queue.jsonl.
entries.consumer: Produced by scripts/generate_and_publish_visibility.py:426-427 (PACKAGES_DIR at :62) and committed by visibility_publish.yml:102 (`git add reports/content_packages/ || true`) on the Tue/Thu cron. No code reads them back; the demonstrated consumer is the run record that points at them: the same script writes the exact path into the immutable history entry at :479 (`"generated_package_path": str(pkg_path)`), and all six paths are present verbatim in the tracked data/strategy/visibility_history.jsonl, one per line. A human auditing a VI publication reaches the payload through that field. Deleting a package would leave a tracked history entry naming a path that no longer exists.
entries.evidence: scripts/generate_and_publish_visibility.py:62, :426-427, :479; data/strategy/visibility_history.jsonl lines 1-6, each carrying `"generated_package_path": "reports/content_packages/vis_00N_generated.json"`; visibility_publish.yml:4-8 (cron), :102. The group is uniform: six sequentially numbered vis_00N items from one producer, one commit mechanism. Rows: vis_001_generated.json through vis_006_generated.json.
entries.canonical: canonical per-item visibility run records, addressed by the history file
entries.action_required: Two notes, neither blocking. (1) The comment at scripts/generate_and_publish_visibility.py:425 justifies the write as being 'for audit trail + --from-package retry'; the audit-trail half is real (:479), the retry half is not — main() at :344-347 exposes only --item-id and --dry-run, and no `--from-package` flag or read-back exists in this script. F-15. (2) The workflow's unbounded `git add reports/content_packages/` (visibility_publish.yml:102) is the mechanism that can sweep in anything else left in that directory — the same mechanism as F-02.

entries.purpose: 4,702 run-scoped artifacts under reports/content_packages/sig-test-001/runs/<uuid4>/ — business_strategy.json, generated.json, editorial_acceptance.json, assignment.json, publication_results.json, run_report.json — each written by one execution of the canonical entrypoint under the fixed test signal id `sig-test-001`. They are test debris, not product artifacts.
entries.consumer: NONE. No workflow, script, test or document reads any path in this group. They are not fixtures: tests build their own inputs and, where they are careful, redirect PACKAGES_DIR to tmp_path (tests/test_research_artifact_lifecycle.py:371-541 does exactly this).
entries.evidence: The producer chain is exact: tests/test_generate_and_publish.py:40 sets `_SIGNAL_ID = 'sig-test-001'`; scripts/generate_and_publish.py:320 defines `PACKAGES_DIR = Path('reports/content_packages')` as a RELATIVE path and :321 mkdirs it at import; :1052 `resolve_run_dir(PACKAGES_DIR, signal_id, run_ctx.run_id)` creates one directory per run id; src/artifacts/__init__.py:9 documents the layout. tests/conftest.py isolates credentials and does not isolate the filesystem, so a suite run from the repository root writes here. Every member of this group matches reports/content_packages/sig-test-001/runs/<uuid>/<one of six fixed filenames> — verified: the 7,796 paths across both test namespaces contain exactly six distinct basenames (business_strategy.json 2422, generated.json 2263, editorial_acceptance.json 1343, assignment.json 1263, publication_results.json 469, run_report.json 36). They entered the repository in a single commit, ffe199a (2026-08-17, 7,830 files, 917,551 insertions), whose subject is a 69-line change to src/reporting/run_report.py. Sample rows: reports/content_packages/sig-test-001/runs/0088997f-d636-401d-8bbb-6e8118f470e7/generated.json, .../010ea427-2e94-45a4-9c8e-3a488ebe4561/generated.json, .../013a0786-dbe8-4d54-8003-4b6e59599dd1/editorial_acceptance.json.
entries.action_required: HIGHEST by volume. Untrack, and ignore the test namespaces in .gitignore using the same explicit pattern data/ already uses. Ongoing cost is real: commit dd54dc5 (#223, a two-line change to src/utils/config_loader.py) shipped 145 files and 864 insertions/deletions, all of it this debris. F-02.
